lines.quote: The prayers of good people got Donald Trump elected two weeks ago.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: A claim about who or what produced the election result, not a reading of the war or the economy.

lines.quote: Wars with Russia and Iran are the counterattack.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Frames war with Iran as a coming reprisal against Trump's election, so the no-war state is threatened.

lines.quote: Mark Levin was at the White House today, lobbying for war with Iran.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Puts blame on a named person for pushing war, which is about who is responsible, not the state of the war.

lines.quote: there is zero credible intelligence that suggests Iran is anywhere near building a bomb
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Disputes the stated case for war with counter-evidence and does not describe the war's state.

lines.quote: which is regime change — young Americans heading back to the Middle East to topple yet another government
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Attributes hidden motives to war advocates rather than reading any measured state.

lines.quote: A war with Iran would amount to a profound betrayal of his supporters.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Judges Trump's loyalty to his voters, which is about his record and loyalties.

lines.quote: The first week of a war with Iran could easily kill thousands of Americans.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: A line about American dead, which is counted and never scored.

lines.quote: It could also collapse our economy, as surging oil prices trigger unmanageable inflation.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Gives a mechanism from war to oil prices to inflation and a wrecked cost of living.

lines.quote: An attack on Iran could very easily become a world war. We'd lose.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: very easily become a world war
lines.why: Predicts that an attack escalates through Iran's allies into a larger lost war.

lines.quote: to box the Trump administration into a regime change war in Iran
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Accuses war advocates of maneuvering the president, a blame claim.

lines.quote: The real divide is between those who casually encourage violence, and those who seek to prevent it — between warmongers and peacemakers.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Sorts people into camps by their stance on the war instead of reading the war itself.

lines.quote: Sean Hannity, Mark Levin, Rupert Murdoch, Ike Perlmutter and Miriam Adelson. At some point they will all have to answer for this
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: will all have to answer for this
lines.why: Names people to blame for pressing Trump toward war.

lines.quote: how the president's enemies are working to destroy MAGA with the war on Iran
lines.subject: Steve Bannon, as relayed by Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Blames the president's enemies for using the war to harm his movement.

lines.quote: Senator Ted Cruz demands regime change in Iran. He's not interested in the details.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Targets a senator's stated position and seriousness, not the war's state.

lines.quote: Thank God.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Reads as relief that the fighting has stopped, the war state improving from US strikes toward a ceasefire.

lines.quote: Thank God Trump brokered a ceasefire.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It reports a ceasefire after the US strikes, a paused state that the war rule scores at -0.5 even though the speaker is relieved.

lines.quote: That's the last thing Mark Levin wanted.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It is about what a named person wanted, not about the war's state.

lines.quote: Our interview with the president of Iran.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It announces an interview and makes no claim about the war's state.

lines.quote: This is Israel's last chance to blow up Iran with America's military
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It frames a coming US war on Iran as the goal of Israel and its allies, with no date given.

lines.quote: naturally the neocons have reached peak hysteria
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It characterizes a faction's motives and temperament rather than the war itself.

lines.quote: So mightily spread abroad your Spirit, that all peoples may be gathered under the banner of the Prince of Peace
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, quoting Newman
lines.why: A prayer for peace posted just after the war began implies the no-war promise is broken.

lines.quote: Israel's war and what it means.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It names the war as under way and frames it as Israel's.

lines.quote: Could this be a religious war designed to rebuild the Third Temple on the ashes of Al Aqsa?
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It frames the current war as a possible religious war, which treats the war as a harm.

lines.quote: how this war changes American politics forever
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, introducing Saagar Enjeti
lines.why: Frames the ongoing war as a lasting break in American politics, which reads as the war frustrating the no-war state.

lines.quote: Pray that the spell breaks and the world is saved.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Describes the war as a spell over the world that needs breaking, so the object is currently frustrated.

lines.quote: it should be illegal to yoke our military to a foreign power in war
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: yoke our military to a foreign power
lines.why: Proposes a legal bar on tying the US military to another country's war, implying Congress's power over war is not working now.

lines.quote: Bret Weinstein on how it happened.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, introducing Bret Weinstein
lines.why: Points to an account of who or what caused the yoking, which is blame and not a reading.

lines.quote: why we actually went to war with Iran
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, introducing Joe Kent
lit: why we actually went to war
lines.why: Implies the real motive differs from the official one, so it is about who is responsible and not about any reading.

lines.quote: ground troops are often followed by tyranny in the country that sends them
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: Gives a mechanism by which sending ground troops damages the sending country, warning against deeper war.

lines.quote: We're spending more a year on the military in adjusted dollars than we did during World War II.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: spending more a year on the military
than we did during World War II
lines.why: States a record of military spending above the WWII level, as a cost of the war economy.

lines.quote: how much is going to Israel
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: how much is going to Israel
lines.why: Asks about Israel's share of the spending, a question of loyalties and blame and not a measured reading.

lines.quote: the Trump administration may be within days of launching a nuclear strike on Iran
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, reporting on the administration
lit: Trump is likely to decide by next weekend
lines.why: It forecasts a sharp escalation of the war, with a decision expected by November 7.

lines.quote: After eight months of conflict, Gulf economies are teetering. So are global energy and fertilizer markets.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: 11 of them were badly damaged in Hormuz
lines.why: It describes the war's damage to energy markets, the oil price being the nearest reading.

lines.quote: Both oppose a negotiated settlement to the war they've so grievously mismanaged
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson on Hegseth and Cooper
lit: pushing to restart major combat operations
lines.why: It assigns blame to named officials for the war's course instead of giving a reading.

lines.quote: After the first nuclear strike, World War Three is inevitable.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lit: free them to use nuclear weapons
lines.why: It argues a causal chain from a US nuclear strike to wider nuclear war, with no date named.

lines.quote: people who have spoken to decision-makers in Iran say there is consensus there that more war is bad for everyone and a deal is worth making
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson, citing people who have spoken to Iranian decision-makers
lit: a deal with Iran can be made
more war is bad for everyone
lines.why: It holds that a negotiated end to the war is still reachable, though not simple.

lines.quote: Neocons and climate hysterics have at least one thing in common: they know nothing about energy.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson
lines.why: It attacks the people involved instead of reading any measured quantity.

lines.quote: Without it, things fall apart. Morgan Downey on the economic effects of American intervention.
lines.subject: Tucker Carlson introducing Morgan Downey
lines.why: It frames the intervention as damaging to the economy through disrupted energy supply.
